Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is an AI-piloted fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets, CMake). On 2026-10-22 Kenneth decided:
- JusPrin checks for its own new versions against the release list of TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin on GitHub.
- Download opens the release page; installing from inside the app comes later.
- JusPrin's first v2 version is 2.0.0, kept separate from OrcaSlicer's SoftFever_VERSION (2.4.2), which 3MF files, profile updates and config upgrades read.

That check is built on branch claude/no-orca-update-window: it reads GitHub's releases API about 10 s after start and then daily. OrcaSlicer's own update check is handed to it through a small GUI_App seam (app_update_check).

The repo's CI is still OrcaSlicer's, so no JusPrin 2.x release exists on GitHub yet; the only releases are JusPrin 1.x (tags v1.3.0, jusprin/v1.4.0) and a stale "nightly-builds" pre-release. Kenneth prefers reports in plain English.

Task:
Design, then build what Kenneth approves: how JusPrin publishes its own app releases and built-in profile updates. JusPrin's update check already reads these releases, but nothing publishes them yet.

Start from:
- `.github/workflows/build_all.yml`, `build_orca.yml` and `publish_release.yml`. Every upload step is gated to `github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer'`. Files are named `OrcaSlicer_…`. `publish_release.yml` only runs for the actor in the repo variable `RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, which is SoftFever. The MSIX step (`scripts/msix`) uses OrcaSlicer's Store identity.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/` on branch `claude/no-orca-update-window`. `Version.hpp` holds JusPrin's version (2.0.0) by hand. `ReleaseFeed.cpp` reads tags `vX.Y.Z` or `jusprin/vX.Y.Z` from GitHub's release list. Drafts and pre-releases are skipped. Release notes come from the release body.
- Profile updates: OrcaSlicer's `PresetUpdater` (`src/slic3r/Utils/PresetUpdater.cpp`, around line 666) asks `AppConfig::profile_update_url()`, which is `check-version.orcaslicer.com/profile`, sending the vendor and `SoftFever_VERSION`. Preferences > Updates' "Update built-in printer and filament profiles" row (`sync_system_preset`) turns it on. Its detail text says "Only the profiles JusPrin ships", which is not what happens.

Answer in plain English, with 2 or 3 options and a recommendation:
1. CI. How the Windows installer and zip, macOS dmg, Linux AppImage and Flatpak get built and attached to a JusPrin GitHub release with a `vX.Y.Z` tag, published by Kenneth.
2. Version. How the tag and `Version.hpp` stay in step: a CI check, or the version derived from the tag.
3. Signing and notarisation. What each platform needs, and what accounts or secrets Kenneth must provide.
4. Profiles. Keep OrcaSlicer's profile server and reword the Preferences row, or publish JusPrin's own profile bundles (for example as release files) and point the updater there. Cover privacy: what each request sends.

Follow `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` for any change to OrcaSlicer-owned workflow or source files: prefer fork-owned workflows or small neutral switches, and record the rebase evidence.

Done means: the recommendation reported. Then, once Kenneth approves, the workflows and code on a branch cut from `claude/no-orca-update-window`, verified by a dry-run release to a draft, without publishing anything public. Don't push or publish a release without Kenneth's explicit go-ahead.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Roaming\Claude\side-session-notes\local_6d12e3c2-d1ec-4939-9214-7be5e8398a61

# JusPrin's own update check: design (2026-10-22)

Design only. Nothing implemented. Worktree read: musing-wing-e808a9 @ 95ab4ea1c2.

## What is true today (checked)

- **JusPrin shows OrcaSlicer's update pop-up.** I ran the prf build (`C:\b\prf\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe`) with a copy of `C:\b\dd3`. Ten seconds in, the "New version of Orca Slicer" window opened and offered "OrcaSlicer V2.5.0 Alpha", with a "Check on GitHub" link to OrcaSlicer. Screenshot: `update-check-orca-dialog-in-jusprin.png` in this folder.
  Why it happens: `GUI_App` startup calls `check_new_version_sf()`. That asks `check-version.orcaslicer.com/latest`. `check_stable_update_only` defaults to false, so the alpha counts, and 2.5.0-alpha is newer than 2.4.2.
- That request also sends OrcaSlicer an install ID (`iid`), plus the version, OS, architecture and OS description. It goes out even in stealth mode. All of this is upstream code: the same text is in upstream/main. Blame can't show it, because the fork's history starts at a squashed root commit, 56eb9a1a46, with no merge-base.
- JusPrin has no version number of its own. `SoftFever_VERSION` is "2.4.2", which is OrcaSlicer's, so Preferences says "JusPrin 2.4.2". JusPrin v1 (origin/main) set it to 1.4.0 and still asked OrcaSlicer's server, according to its code. I did not run v1.
- JusPrin's GitHub releases: `jusprin/v1.4.0` (2025-10-19, the latest stable), v1.3.0, and older `v*` tags. There is also a rolling `nightly-builds` pre-release with Windows exe and zip, macOS dmg, AppImage and flatpak files. No v2 release yet. The CI publish steps are gated to the OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer repo.
- MSIX: `scripts/msix` and its CI step are OrcaSlicer's, and the identity is OrcaSlicer's. JusPrin ships no MSIX.
- Canvas boards: "Updates" shows "JusPrin [VERSION]", "Up to date · checked [TIME]" and [Check now]. "Updates · new version available" shows "JusPrin [NEW] is available", "You have [VERSION]. Your projects and settings carry over.", [Download] and [What's new], plus a dot on the Updates nav item. The built page has the "available" card and the dot, but no checked line and no Check now.

## Recommendation: option 1

JusPrin's own small check, reading GitHub releases. OrcaSlicer's check is handed over through one neutral hook.

- Source: `GET https://api.github.com/repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases?per_page=30`. Skip drafts and pre-releases. Tags are `v<semver>` or `jusprin/v<semver>`. Pick the highest version above the running one. Its `html_url` is the Download and What's new link.
- When: at startup, if the last check is more than 24 h old (OrcaSlicer's startup call reaches it through the hook). Once a day while JusPrin stays open. Any time from Check now. Timeouts 5 s connect, 10 s total.
- Shown:
  - In Preferences, as on the canvas.
  - On Home, one quiet strip: "JusPrin X is available." with Download, What's new and ×. × hides it until a newer version.
  - Nothing modal, nothing in projects or chat. The agent never downloads or installs.
- Test versions: no. A build that is itself a test version (2.1.0-beta1) is told about newer test versions. Nightly builds are never offered.
- Offline or a failed check: silent. Preferences says "Couldn't check just now · last checked …". The next try is at the next start or 24 h later. A failure is recorded as a failure, never as "up to date". Don't copy OrcaSlicer's `catch (...) {}`.
- Privacy: a plain GET with no install ID and no OS details. GitHub sees the IP address and the User-Agent "JusPrin/<version>". Add a check row in "What to check for", on by default: "New JusPrin versions — Once a day JusPrin asks GitHub for its list of releases. GitHub sees your IP address, as with any web page. Nothing about you or your projects is sent." It is also off when stealth mode is on.
- Platforms:
  - Windows exe and zip, macOS dmg and AppImage: same check; Download opens the release page.
  - MSIX, if it ever ships: no check, and the page says "Updates come from the Microsoft Store" (use upstream's `is_running_in_msix()`).
  - Flatpak from a store, later: same idea, using `/.flatpak-info` as upstream does.

## Smallest code change

1. The OrcaSlicer-owned files are touched in one place, three lines, all additive:
   - `GUI_App.hpp`: `std::function<void(int by_user)> app_update_check; // runs instead of the built-in check when set`
   - First line of `GUI_App::check_new_version_sf()`: `if (app_update_check) { app_update_check(by_user); return; }`
   - The function has had one upstream commit since 2026-01. JusPrin sets the hook in `JusPrin::attach_shell()`, which runs in the MainFrame constructor, before the startup CallAfter.
   - Classic view's "Check for updates" menu item then runs JusPrin's check instead of doing nothing.
   - The rebase simulation must be run when this is implemented.
2. New files `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/UpdateCheck.{hpp,cpp}`. They hold a pure `choose_update(releases json, running version)`, tested in tests/jusprin, and the request plus app_config state: version, url, checked time, last result, dismissed version. They borrow upstream's `Http` and `Semver`.
3. `JUSPRIN_VERSION` goes in a fork-owned cmake file. Leave `SoftFever_VERSION` alone: profiles, the `user_backup-v<ver>` folder and the conf "version" depend on it. Kenneth picks the first v2 number, which must be above 1.4.0.
4. In `PreferencesWindow.cpp`, `known_update()` reads UpdateCheck, and a `check_now` effect is added. Preferences.tsx and protocol.ts get the checked line, Check now, the failure line and the toggle.
5. The Home strip needs a canvas board first.

## Options not chosen

- **Option 2: reuse OrcaSlicer's check.** Point its `version_check_url` setting at JusPrin's GitHub API and bind `EVT_SLIC3R_VERSION_ONLINE` later so JusPrin's handler swallows the event. It adds the fewest lines. But it sends the install ID and OS details to GitHub on every check, and it keeps OrcaSlicer's test-version logic and its by-user dialogs. It also depends on the order wx calls event handlers in, which upstream can change with no merge conflict.
- **Option 3: a JusPrin feed on Obico's server.** It gives the most control: pulling a bad release, staged rollout, per-platform links, a message. But it needs a server and a step to keep it in sync with GitHub releases, and the privacy line must name Obico. Option 1 keeps the URL in one constant, so moving later is cheap.

## 2026-10-22 follow-up: Kenneth's decisions and the canvas design

Kenneth's decisions:
- Use JusPrin's own GitHub release list.
- Don't reuse OrcaSlicer's update window; design JusPrin's own experience on the Preferences page.

Canvas (JusPrin v2, version 102, page "Agent setup & Preferences", new row "Updates · from Check now to Restart and install"):
- prefs-window.dc.html now has eight update states: current, checking, failed, available, downloading, ready, downloadFailed, store.
- "Stable releases only" is gone. A new check row "New JusPrin versions" carries the privacy text.
- New boards: prefs-updates-{checking,failed,downloading,ready,download-failed,store,available-dark}.
- The existing prefs-updates-available board moved into the new row.
- In Play, Check now → checking → available → Download and install → downloading → ready.

In-app download and install is new scope:
- The file is checked against the checksum GitHub publishes for each release file.
- Windows runs the installer after quitting. macOS opens the disk image. Portable and Flatpak copies fall back to the GitHub link.

## 2026-10-22, built: what landed and where

Branches (not pushed):
- `claude/no-orca-update-window`:
  - a6cf684da9: OrcaSlicer's update window filtered.
  - 8a572b924b: JusPrin's own check (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/), version 2.0.0, tests.
- `claude/prefs-update-check`: claude/musing-wing-e808a9 plus the commit above, merged (946b79ca29), then:
  - 0f33095b30: Preferences > Updates wiring.
  - c46771fa7d: release-notes styling.

Where things are:
- Screenshots from the running app are in this folder: updates-available.png, updates-checking.png, updates-couldnt-check.png, updates-up-to-date.png.
- The fake GitHub server and the scripts that drive the app are in my scratchpad: fake-github.js, set-conf.js (rewrites JusPrin2.conf with its MD5 line), cdp.js and shoot-updates.ps1.
- The test hook is the AppConfig key `jusprin_update_feed_url`.

Known, not mine: on a Windows checkout with autocrlf, AgentUI's projectInstructions.test.ts and skills.test.ts fail, because the CRLF line endings don't match the pinned LF text.

# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit

**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.

**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.

**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
owned by Plater's event handler.

Historical measurements and the incidents behind several of these rules are in the [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) and, for the spike era, in the [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

name: Build all

on:
  push:
    branches:
     - main
     - release/*
     - belt-printer
    paths:
     - 'deps/**'
     - 'src/**'
     - '**/CMakeLists.txt'
     - 'version.inc'
     - 'localization/**'
     - 'resources/**'
     - ".github/workflows/build_*.yml"
     - 'scripts/flatpak/**'
     - 'scripts/msix/**'
     - 'tests/**'

  pull_request:
    branches:
     - main
     - release/*
    paths:
     - 'deps/**'
     - 'deps_src/**'
     - 'src/**'
     - '**/CMakeLists.txt'
     - 'version.inc'
     - ".github/workflows/build_*.yml"
     - 'build_linux.sh'
     - 'build_release_vs.bat'
     - 'build_release_vs2022.bat'
     - 'build_release_macos.sh'
     - 'scripts/flatpak/**'
     - 'scripts/msix/**'
     - 'tests/**'


  schedule:
      - cron: '0 17 * * *' # run once a day at 1 AM Singapore time (UTC+8)

  workflow_dispatch: # allows for manual dispatch
    inputs:
      build-deps-only:
        description: 'Only build dependencies (bypasses caching)'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
  

jobs:
  build_linux:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Build both arches on every event (PRs included), through the same
      # build_check_cache -> build_deps -> build_orca chain (the AppImage).
      # aarch64 always uses the GitHub-hosted arm runner (there is no arm
      # self-hosted server). amd64's empty arch is load-bearing: it keeps the
      # historical 'linux-clang' deps cache key and the unsuffixed asset names.
      matrix:
        include:
          - arch: ""
            os: ${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED && 'orca-lnx-server' || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
          - arch: "aarch64"
            os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # Don't run scheduled builds on forks:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer') }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_check_cache.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      build-deps-only: ${{ inputs.build-deps-only || false }}
    secrets: inherit
  build_windows:
    name: Build Windows ${{ matrix.arch }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - arch: x64
            os: windows-latest
          - arch: arm64
            os: windows-11-arm
    # Don't run scheduled builds on forks:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer') }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_check_cache.yml
    with:
      # Self-hosted runner is x64-only; ARM64 always uses the GitHub-hosted runner.
      os: ${{ (matrix.arch == 'x64' && vars.SELF_HOSTED) && 'orca-win-server' || matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      build-deps-only: ${{ inputs.build-deps-only || false }}
      force-build: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    secrets: inherit
  build_macos_arch:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        arch:
          - arm64
          - x86_64
    # Don't run scheduled builds on forks:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && (github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer') }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_check_cache.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED && 'orca-macos-arm64' || 'macos-14' }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      build-deps-only: ${{ inputs.build-deps-only || false }}
      force-build: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    secrets: inherit
  build_macos_universal:
    name: Build macOS Universal
    needs: build_macos_arch
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.build_macos_arch.result == 'success' && !inputs.build-deps-only && (github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer') }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_orca.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED && 'orca-macos-arm64' || 'macos-14' }}
      arch: universal
      macos-combine-only: true
    secrets: inherit
  unit_tests:
    name: Unit Tests
    # Tests are built on the aarch64 leg by default (faster GitHub arm runner),
    # so run them there; self-hosted builds them on the amd64 server instead.
    runs-on: ${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED && 'orca-lnx-server' || 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' }}
    needs: build_linux
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && success() }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            .github
            scripts
            tests
      - name: Apt-Install Dependencies
        if: ${{ !vars.SELF_HOSTED }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps
      - name: Restore Test Artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: ${{ github.sha }}-tests
      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"  # use most recent 4.3.x version
          useLocalCache: true         # <--= Use the local cache (default is 'false').
          useCloudCache: true
      - name: Unpackage and Run Unit Tests
        timeout-minutes: 20
        run: |
          tar -xvf build_tests.tar
          scripts/run_unit_tests.sh
      - name: Upload Test Logs
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        with:
          name: unit-test-logs
          path: build/tests/**/*.log
      - name: Publish Test Results
        if: always()
        uses: EnricoMi/publish-unit-test-result-action@v2
        with:
          files: "ctest_results.xml"
      - name: Delete Test Artifact
        if: success()
        uses: geekyeggo/delete-artifact@v6
        with:
          name: ${{ github.sha }}-tests
  flatpak:
    name: "Flatpak"
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/flathub-infra/flatpak-github-actions:gnome-50
      options: --privileged
      volumes:
        - /usr/local/lib/android:/usr/local/lib/android
        - /usr/share/dotnet:/usr/share/dotnet
        - /opt/ghc:/opt/ghc1
        - /usr/local/share/boost:/usr/local/share/boost1
        - /opt/hostedtoolcache:/opt/hostedtoolcache1
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        variant:
          - arch: x86_64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
          - arch: aarch64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # Don't run scheduled builds on forks; skip entirely on self-hosted runners
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && !vars.SELF_HOSTED && (github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer') }}

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.variant.runner }}
    env:
      date:
      ver:
      ver_pure:
      # Belt-printer nightlies share the main nightly release but carry a `_belt`
      # suffix so they never overwrite the main assets.
      nightly_suffix: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/belt-printer' && '_belt' || '' }}
    steps:
    - name: "Remove unneeded stuff to free disk space"
      run:
        rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android/* /usr/share/dotnet/* /opt/ghc1/* "/usr/local/share/boost1/*" /opt/hostedtoolcache1/*
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - name: Get the version and date
      run: |
        ver_pure=$(grep 'set(SoftFever_VERSION' version.inc | cut -d '"' -f2)
        if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "pull_request" ]]; then
          ver="PR-${{ github.event.number }}"
          git_commit_hash="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
        else
          ver=V$ver_pure
          git_commit_hash="${{ github.sha }}"
        fi
        echo "ver=$ver" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        echo "ver_pure=$ver_pure" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        echo "date=$(date +'%Y%m%d')" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        echo "git_commit_hash=$git_commit_hash" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      shell: bash
    # Manage flatpak-builder cache externally so PRs restore but never upload
    - name: Restore flatpak-builder cache
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
      with:
        path: .flatpak-builder
        key: flatpak-builder-${{ matrix.variant.arch }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        restore-keys: flatpak-builder-${{ matrix.variant.arch }}-
    - name: Save/restore flatpak-builder cache
      if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
      uses: actions/cache@v5
      with:
        path: .flatpak-builder
        key: flatpak-builder-${{ matrix.variant.arch }}-${{ github.sha }}
        restore-keys: flatpak-builder-${{ matrix.variant.arch }}-
    - name: Disable debug info for faster CI builds
      run: |
        sed -i '/^build-options:/a\  no-debuginfo: true\n  strip: true' \
          scripts/flatpak/com.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer.yml
      shell: bash
    - name: Inject git commit hash into Flatpak manifest
      run: |
        sed -i "/name: OrcaSlicer/{n;s|buildsystem: simple|buildsystem: simple\n    build-options:\n      env:\n        git_commit_hash: \"$git_commit_hash\"|}" \
          scripts/flatpak/com.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer.yml
      shell: bash
    - uses: flatpak/flatpak-github-actions/flatpak-builder@master
      with:
        bundle: OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_${{ env.ver }}_${{ matrix.variant.arch }}.flatpak
        manifest-path: scripts/flatpak/com.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer.yml
        cache: false
        arch: ${{ matrix.variant.arch }}
        upload-artifact: false
    - name: Upload artifacts Flatpak
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_${{ env.ver }}_${{ matrix.variant.arch }}.flatpak
        path: '/__w/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_${{ env.ver }}_${{ matrix.variant.arch }}.flatpak'
    - name: Deploy Flatpak to nightly release
      if: github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/belt-printer')
      uses: WebFreak001/deploy-nightly@v3.2.0
      with:
        upload_url: https://uploads.github.com/repos/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/releases/137995723/assets{?name,label}
        release_id: 137995723
        asset_path: /__w/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_${{ env.ver }}_${{ matrix.variant.arch }}.flatpak
        asset_name: OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_nightly${{ env.nightly_suffix }}_${{ matrix.variant.arch }}.flatpak
        asset_content_type: application/octet-stream
        max_releases: 1 # optional, if there are more releases than this matching the asset_name, the oldest ones are going to be deleted

result.output:
on:
    workflow_call:
      inputs:
        cache-key:
          required: false
          type: string
        cache-path:
          required: false
          type: string
        os:
          required: true
          type: string
        arch:
          required: false
          type: string
        macos-combine-only:
          required: false
          type: boolean
          default: false

jobs:
  build_orca:
    name: Build OrcaSlicer
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    env:
      date:
      ver:
      ver_pure:
      ubuntu-ver: '2404'
      ubuntu-ver-str: '_Ubuntu2404'
      ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY: ${{ secrets.ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY }}
      # Branches whose builds are published to the nightly release. The
      # belt-printer branch ships alongside main but its assets carry a `_belt`
      # suffix (nightly_suffix) so they never overwrite the main nightly assets.
      deploy_nightly: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/belt-printer' }}
      nightly_suffix: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/belt-printer' && '_belt' || '' }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: load cached deps
        if: ${{ !(runner.os == 'macOS' && inputs.macos-combine-only) }}
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ inputs.cache-path }}
          key: ${{ inputs.cache-key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        # The windows-11-arm runner needs CMake <= 3.31 (handled in the next step).
        if: ${{ !(runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') }}
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"  # use most recent 4.3.x version
          useLocalCache: true         # <--= Use the local cache (default is 'false').
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: Install CMake 3.31.x (Windows ARM64)
        # windows-11-arm ships CMake 4.x, which removed pre-3.5 policy
        # compatibility AND has incomplete ASM_ARMASM linker modules
        # (breaks Boost.Context on ARM64). Pin to the last 3.x release.
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ver = "3.31.6"
          $url = "https://github.com/Kitware/CMake/releases/download/v$ver/cmake-$ver-windows-arm64.zip"
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\cmake.zip"
          Expand-Archive -Path "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\cmake.zip" -DestinationPath "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\cmake" -Force
          $cmakeBin = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\cmake\cmake-$ver-windows-arm64\bin"
          if (-not (Test-Path "$cmakeBin\cmake.exe")) { throw "cmake.exe not found at $cmakeBin" }
          Add-Content -Path $env:GITHUB_PATH -Value $cmakeBin

      - name: Get the version and date on Ubuntu and macOS
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          ver_pure=$(grep 'set(SoftFever_VERSION' version.inc | cut -d '"' -f2)
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "pull_request" ]]; then
            ver="PR-${{ github.event.number }}"
            git_commit_hash="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          else
            ver=V$ver_pure
            git_commit_hash=""
          fi
          echo "ver=$ver" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "ver_pure=$ver_pure" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "date=$(date +'%Y%m%d')" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "git_commit_hash=$git_commit_hash" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          # Per-arch Linux AppImage naming: amd64 keeps the historical unsuffixed
          # name (arch_suffix empty). Unused on macOS/Windows.
          if [ '${{ inputs.arch }}' = 'aarch64' ]; then
            echo "arch_suffix=_aarch64" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          fi
        shell: bash

      - name: Get the version and date on Windows
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          $date = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd'
          $ref = "${{ github.ref }}"
          $eventName = "${{ github.event_name }}"
          $prNumber = "${{ github.event.number }}"

          if ($eventName -eq 'pull_request') {
              $ver = "PR" + $prNumber
              $git_commit_hash = "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          } else {
              $versionContent = Get-Content version.inc -Raw
              if ($versionContent -match 'set\(SoftFever_VERSION "(.*?)"\)') {
                  $ver = $matches[1]
              }
              $ver = "V$ver"
              $git_commit_hash = ""
          }

          echo "ver=$ver" | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8
          echo "date=$date" | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8
          echo "git_commit_hash=$git_commit_hash" | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8
          echo "date: ${{ env.date }} version: ${{ env.ver }}"
        shell: pwsh

#   Mac
      - name: Install tools mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && !inputs.macos-combine-only
        run: |
          if [ -z "${{ vars.SELF_HOSTED }}" ]; then
            brew install libtool
            brew list
          fi
          mkdir -p ${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}

      - name: Free disk space
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && !inputs.macos-combine-only && !vars.SELF_HOSTED
        run: |
          df -hI /dev/disk3s1s1
          sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "Xcode_15.4.app" -exec rm -rf {} +
          sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*
          df -hI /dev/disk3s1s1

      - name: Build slicer mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && !inputs.macos-combine-only
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x ${{ !vars.SELF_HOSTED && '-1' || '' }} -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15

      - name: Pack macOS app bundle ${{ inputs.arch }}
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && !inputs.macos-combine-only
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          tar -czvf OrcaSlicer_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}_${{ github.sha }}.tar.gz -C build/${{ inputs.arch }} OrcaSlicer

      - name: Upload macOS app bundle ${{ inputs.arch }}
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && !inputs.macos-combine-only
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: OrcaSlicer_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}_${{ github.sha }}
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/OrcaSlicer_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}_${{ github.sha }}.tar.gz

      - name: Download macOS app bundles
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && inputs.macos-combine-only
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: OrcaSlicer_Mac_bundle_*_${{ github.sha }}
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/mac_bundles

      - name: Extract macOS app bundles
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && inputs.macos-combine-only
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/arm64 build/x86_64
          arm_bundle=$(find "${{ github.workspace }}/mac_bundles/OrcaSlicer_Mac_bundle_arm64_${{ github.sha }}" -name '*.tar.gz' -print -quit)
          x86_bundle=$(find "${{ github.workspace }}/mac_bundles/OrcaSlicer_Mac_bundle_x86_64_${{ github.sha }}" -name '*.tar.gz' -print -quit)
          tar -xzvf "$arm_bundle" -C "${{ github.workspace }}/build/arm64"
          tar -xzvf "$x86_bundle" -C "${{ github.workspace }}/build/x86_64"

      - name: Build universal mac app bundle
        if: runner.os == 'macOS' && inputs.macos-combine-only
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x ${{ !vars.SELF_HOSTED && '-1' || '' }} -a universal -t 10.15

 # Thanks to RaySajuuk, it's working now
      - name: Sign app and notary
        if: github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/belt-printer' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/release/')) && runner.os == 'macOS' && inputs.macos-combine-only
        working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
          CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
        run: |
          # Load the `retry` helper (retries flaky commands such as `hdiutil create`).
          source ${{ github.workspace }}/scripts/retry.sh
          CERTIFICATE_PATH=$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12
          KEYCHAIN_PATH=$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output $CERTIFICATE_PATH
          security create-keychain -p $KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD $KEYCHAIN_PATH
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 $KEYCHAIN_PATH
          security unlock-keychain -p $KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD $KEYCHAIN_PATH
          # Set the temporary keychain as the default to prevent codesign from accessing the locked login keychain
          security default-keychain -s "$KEYCHAIN_PATH"
          security import $CERTIFICATE_PATH -P $P12_PASSWORD -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k $KEYCHAIN_PATH
          security list-keychain -d user -s $KEYCHAIN_PATH
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k $P12_PASSWORD $KEYCHAIN_PATH
          codesign --deep --force --verbose --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements ${{ github.workspace }}/scripts/disable_validation.entitlements --sign "$CERTIFICATE_ID" ${{ github.workspace }}/build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app
          # Sign OrcaSlicer_profile_validator.app if it exists
          if [ -f "${{ github.workspace }}/build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_profile_validator.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer_profile_validator" ]; then
            codesign --deep --force --verbose --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements ${{ github.workspace }}/scripts/disable_validation.entitlements --sign "$CERTIFICATE_ID" ${{ github.workspace }}/build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_profile_validator.app
          fi
          
          # Create main OrcaSlicer DMG without the profile validator helper
          mkdir -p ${{ github.workspace }}/build/universal/OrcaSlicer_dmg
          rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/build/universal/OrcaSlicer_dmg/*

name: Publish to draft release

# Manually pulls the platform binaries produced by a "Build all" run and uploads
# them to an existing DRAFT release. Decoupled from the build so you can test a
# build first, then publish exactly that run's artifacts once you're happy.
#
# Trigger: Actions tab -> "Publish to draft release" -> Run workflow.
# Locked to a single person: the first step aborts unless the actor matches the
# `RELEASE_PUBLISHER` repo variable (set to "SoftFever"). To allow someone else,
# change that variable: gh variable set RELEASE_PUBLISHER --body "<login>".

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run_id:
        description: 'Run ID of the "Build all" workflow to pull binaries from (the number in the Actions run URL)'
        required: true
        type: string
      tag:
        description: 'Tag of the draft release to upload to (e.g. v2.4.0)'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write   # upload release assets
  actions: read     # download artifacts from another run

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Publish binaries to draft release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      RUN_ID: ${{ inputs.run_id }}
      TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Restrict to the release publisher
        env:
          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.RELEASE_PUBLISHER }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::RELEASE_PUBLISHER repo variable is not set."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ github.actor }}" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may run this workflow (you are @${{ github.actor }})."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Authorized: @${{ github.actor }}"

      - name: Verify target is a draft release
        run: |
          if ! gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json isDraft >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::Release '$TAG' not found. Create the draft (with this tag) first."
            exit 1
          fi
          is_draft=$(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft')
          if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::error::Release '$TAG' is published, not a draft. Aborting to avoid touching a live release."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Verify source build run
        run: |
          info=$(gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json workflowName,conclusion,headBranch)
          name=$(echo "$info" | jq -r '.workflowName')
          conclusion=$(echo "$info" | jq -r '.conclusion')
          branch=$(echo "$info" | jq -r '.headBranch')
          echo "Source run #$RUN_ID: '$name' on '$branch' (conclusion: $conclusion)"
          if [ "$conclusion" != "success" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Source run did not conclude 'success' ($conclusion). Some assets may be missing."
          fi

      - name: Download release artifacts from build run
        run: |
          # Windows_V* (not Windows_*) keeps the MSIX Store artifact out: it goes to Partner Center, not GitHub releases.
          gh run download "$RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --dir artifacts \
            -p 'OrcaSlicer_Windows_V*' \
            -p 'OrcaSlicer_Mac_universal_*' \
            -p 'OrcaSlicer_Linux_ubuntu_*' \
            -p 'OrcaSlicer-Linux-flatpak_*' \
            -p 'PDB'
          echo "Downloaded artifact folders:"
          ls -1 artifacts

      - name: Assemble release assets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p upload

          # gh run download auto-extracts each artifact into a folder, so the inner
          # binaries are already unzipped. Copy the inner binary for each platform.
          # -type f is required (some artifact *folders* are named "*.flatpak").

          # Windows installers (x64 + arm64): the .exe inside each installer
          # artifact, NOT the orca-slicer.exe in the portable app folder. CPack
          # now bakes the arch into the filename (…_x64.exe / …_arm64.exe), so
          # copy them straight through.
          find artifacts -type f -name '*.exe' -path '*OrcaSlicer_Windows_V*' ! -path '*_portable*' -exec cp -v {} upload/ \;
          # macOS universal DMG (profile-validator DMG isn't downloaded).
          find artifacts -type f -name '*.dmg' -path '*OrcaSlicer_Mac_universal_*' -exec cp -v {} upload/ \;
          # Linux AppImage.

name: Check Cache

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      os:
        required: true
        type: string
      arch:
        required: false
        type: string
      build-deps-only:
        required: false
        type: boolean
      force-build:
        required: false
        type: boolean
  
jobs:
  check_cache: # determines if there is a cache and outputs variables used in caching process
    name: Check Cache
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    outputs:
      cache-key: ${{ steps.set_outputs.outputs.cache-key }}
      cache-path: ${{ steps.set_outputs.outputs.cache-path }}
      valid-cache: ${{ steps.cache_deps.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'
        
      - name: set outputs
        id: set_outputs
        env:
          # Keep macOS/Windows cache keys architecture-specific. amd64 Linux passes
          # no arch (key stays 'linux-clang', preserving the existing cache);
          # aarch64 gets its own 'linux-clang-aarch64' key.
          cache-os: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && format('macos-{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
          # ARM64 builds use the build-arm64 tree (see build_release_vs.bat); x64/other use build.
          dep-folder-name: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
          output-cmd: ${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '$env:GITHUB_OUTPUT' || '"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"'}}
        run: |
          echo cache-key=${{ env.cache-os }}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }} >> ${{ env.output-cmd }}
          echo cache-path=${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build${{ env.dep-folder-name }} >> ${{ env.output-cmd }}
            
      - name: load cache
        id: cache_deps
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.set_outputs.outputs.cache-path }}
          key: ${{ steps.set_outputs.outputs.cache-key }}
          lookup-only: true
        
  build_deps: # call next step
    name: Build Deps
    needs: [check_cache]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    with:
      cache-key: ${{ needs.check_cache.outputs.cache-key }}
      cache-path: ${{ needs.check_cache.outputs.cache-path }}
      valid-cache: ${{ needs.check_cache.outputs.valid-cache == 'true' }}
      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
      build-deps-only: ${{ inputs.build-deps-only }}
      force-build: ${{ inputs.force-build }}
    secrets: inherit

          installers-regex: '\.exe$'

# Check if required arguments are provided
if [ "$#" -lt 3 ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 VERSION NUMBER VENDOR1 [VENDOR2 ...]"
    echo "Example: $0 2.3.0 1 OrcaFilamentLibrary BBL"
    exit 1
fi

# Get version and number from arguments
VERSION="$1"
NUMBER="$2"
shift 2  # Remove first two arguments, leaving only vendor names

# Set paths
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/../resources/profiles"
ORIGINAL_DIR="$(pwd)"
OUTPUT_FILE="orcaslicer-profiles_ota_${VERSION}.${NUMBER}.zip"
TEMP_DIR="/tmp/orca_profiles_$$"  # Use PID to make temp dir unique

# Check if resources directory exists
if [ ! -d "$RESOURCES_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Error: Profiles directory not found at $RESOURCES_DIR"
    exit 1
fi

# Create temporary directory with profiles root folder
mkdir -p "$TEMP_DIR/profiles"

# Process each vendor
for VENDOR in "$@"; do
    echo "Processing vendor: $VENDOR"
    
    # Copy JSON file if it exists
    if [ -f "$RESOURCES_DIR/$VENDOR.json" ]; then
        cp "$RESOURCES_DIR/$VENDOR.json" "$TEMP_DIR/profiles/"
        echo "Added $VENDOR.json"
    else
        echo "Warning: $VENDOR.json not found"

# JusPrin release publishing: design (2026-10-22)

Design only, waiting for Kenneth. Branch cut: `claude/jusprin-release-publishing` from `claude/no-orca-update-window` @ c18332e55c (worktree great-blackburn-283b43). Nothing pushed, nothing built.

## Checked facts

- JusPrin releases on GitHub: jusprin/v1.4.0 (Win installer + zip, Mac universal dmg, Linux AppImage), v1.3.0 and older, plus the `nightly-builds` pre-release. All by kennethjiang. No v2.
- v1 CI edited OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml in place (repo gate, JusPrin_ names, release id 239202561). v1 notarised Mac builds with secrets named BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64, P12_PASSWORD, KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD, MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID, APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID, APP_PWD. v1 Windows builds were unsigned. Could not list the repo's secrets (no gh CLI, no token here).
- Upstream build_orca.yml: 77 upstream commits since 2026-01. Editing it in place is the expensive kind of fork ownership.
- The v2 tree still packages as OrcaSlicer: CPack name/registry key/install dir "OrcaSlicer", vendor SoftFever, installer file OrcaSlicer_Windows_Installer_V2.4.2_x64.exe, CPACK_NSIS_ENABLE_UNINSTALL_BEFORE_INSTALL ON (so the installer would remove a real OrcaSlicer install); macOS bundle OrcaSlicer.app, CFBundleIdentifier com.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer, short version 2.4.2; Flatpak app-id com.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer (19 references in the manifest); Linux desktop file com.orcaslicer.OrcaSlicer.desktop; URL schemes orcaslicer://. v1 used CPack name/key "JusPrin", vendor obico, Xcode bundle id io.obico.jusprin.
- Data dir is JusPrin2 (SLIC3R_APP_KEY), so user data does not collide.
- The build needs npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt). Hosted runners have Node; the Flatpak container does not, and flatpak-builder has no network.
- workflow_dispatch workflows must exist on the default branch (main = v1) to be runnable.
- Profile updates: `GET check-version.orcaslicer.com/profile?vendor=<maker>&orca_version=2.4.2`, User-Agent `JusPrin/2.4.2`, no install ID. Sent at startup for the selected printer's maker (only if sync_system_preset and not stealth), and on every switch to a new maker via Tab.cpp:2123 -> check_vendor_update, which checks neither the row nor stealth mode.
- The server answered 404 for BBL, Creality, Prusa at 2.3.0, 2.4.0, 2.4.1, 2.4.2, 2.5.0: it serves nothing today.
- JusPrin's resources/profiles equal OrcaSlicer v2.4.2's except Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg.

## Recommendation (see chat report for the plain-English version)

- CI: fork-owned `jusprin_release.yml` (workflow_dispatch, Environment "release" with Kenneth as required reviewer) that reuses upstream's reusable build_check_cache.yml, then fork-owned package jobs rename/sign/notarise and upload to a draft release. No upstream workflow edits.
- Identity: one added line in CMakeLists.txt before include(CPack): include a fork-owned packaging.cmake that sets the JusPrin CPack identity and version. Mac bundle id/name/version set with PlistBuddy in the package job before signing.
- Version: Version.hpp is the one source; the workflow names the draft vX.Y.Z from it; the tag is created when Kenneth publishes.
- Signing: Mac with v1's Apple secrets (re-check validity); Windows unsigned for 2.0.0 or Azure Trusted Signing; Linux checksums only.
- Profiles: turn off (profiles arrive with each JusPrin release), plus a 2-line seam so check_vendor_update obeys the row and stealth mode.

I've done the research but not the build: nothing is pushed or built, and nothing has gone to GitHub yet. One problem has to be fixed before any release. JusPrin 2 still packages itself as OrcaSlicer, so its Windows installer would remove a real OrcaSlicer install. The branch is `claude/jusprin-release-publishing`, cut from `claude/no-orca-update-window`, and my notes are in [release-publishing-design.md](C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Roaming\Claude\side-session-notes\local_6d12e3c2-d1ec-4939-9214-7be5e8398a61\release-publishing-design.md).

## First, a blocker

JusPrin 2's packages still claim to be OrcaSlicer:
- **Windows:** the installer is named and registered as "OrcaSlicer" by "SoftFever". It is also set to uninstall the previous "OrcaSlicer" before installing, so on a machine that has OrcaSlicer, installing JusPrin would remove it.
- **macOS:** the app is `OrcaSlicer.app` with OrcaSlicer's app ID.
- **Flatpak:** the app ID is OrcaSlicer's, so it would clash with OrcaSlicer from Flathub.
- **Shown version:** "2.4.2" everywhere.

Your data folders don't clash, because JusPrin keeps its own. JusPrin 1.x had fixed this by renaming; that change didn't carry over to v2.

**Fix:** one added line in OrcaSlicer's `CMakeLists.txt`, just before it packages, that loads a JusPrin-owned settings file. That file sets the Windows name, publisher, version and install folder. On macOS, the release job renames the app and sets its ID and version just before signing, so OrcaSlicer's files stay untouched.

**Your call:** should 2.0.0 replace JusPrin 1.x on Windows (same install entry, "JusPrin"), or install alongside it ("JusPrin 2")? I lean towards replace: your 1.x settings stay on disk either way.

## 1. Building and attaching the files

- **A. JusPrin's own release workflow (recommended).** A new workflow, started by hand, reuses OrcaSlicer's build steps unchanged. JusPrin-owned steps then rename the files to `JusPrin_…_V2.0.0`, sign them, and upload them to a draft release. You review the draft and click Publish yourself. Only you can run it: its secrets sit in a GitHub "release" environment that needs your approval.
- **B. Edit OrcaSlicer's workflows in place, as JusPrin 1.x did.** OrcaSlicer changed its main build file 77 times this year, so every rebase means conflicts. The 1.x history already has "Merge error" commits from this.
- **C. Copy OrcaSlicer's whole build into a JusPrin file.** No conflicts, but OrcaSlicer's build fixes would stop reaching us without anyone noticing.

For 2.0.0 I'd ship what 1.4.0 shipped:
- Windows installer and zip
- macOS universal dmg
- Linux AppImage
- Windows ARM and Linux ARM cost almost nothing to add.

I'd move **Flatpak** to 2.0.1. It needs its own app ID, and its build environment has no Node or network, which JusPrin's web pages need to build.

Two practical points:
- A hand-started workflow only shows a Run button if it also exists on `main`, which is still the 1.x branch. So I'd add the file there too, or you switch the default branch to v2.
- The dry run will also be the first CI build of v2 ever, so expect some fixes.

## 2. Keeping the tag and the version in step

- **A. Keep `Version.hpp` by hand and have CI fail if the tag doesn't match.** Simple, but the version is typed in two places.
- **B. Take the version from the tag.** The tag has to exist before the build, so it goes public before you've reviewed anything, and builds made from the source alone show the wrong version.
- **C. Make the tag from the version (recommended).** `Version.hpp` stays the only place the number lives. The workflow reads it and names the draft `v2.0.0`. GitHub only creates the tag when you click Publish. CI refuses to build if that version is already released or isn't higher than the latest one. The installer and the Mac app read the same number.

Drafts never reach users: GitHub's public release list, which the in-app check reads, leaves them out.

## 3. Signing

**macOS (needed, or the Mac refuses to open the app):**
- You need Obico's Apple Developer account ($99/yr), a "Developer ID Application" certificate exported as a .p12 file with its password, and notarisation login details.
- JusPrin 1.4.0 was notarised using secrets named `BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64`, `P12_PASSWORD`, `KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD`, `MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID`, `APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT`, `TEAM_ID` and `APP_PWD`, so they are probably still in the repo.
- I couldn't check from here. Please confirm they still work; the app-specific password is the one most likely to have lapsed.

**Windows (optional; 1.x shipped unsigned):**
- **Unsigned:** people see "Windows protected your PC" and must click More info, then Run anyway.
- **Azure Trusted Signing (recommended when you're ready):**
  - About $10 a month, plus a one-time check of Obico's company identity that takes a few days.
  - You'd give me an Azure tenant ID, client ID, client secret, and the signing account and profile names.
  - The installer and the exe in the zip get signed after the build, so OrcaSlicer's build files stay untouched.
- **A certificate from a vendor (~$200–500 a year):** works, but costs more and is more fiddly in CI.

**Linux:** nothing is required. I'd attach a SHA256 checksum file, and GitHub also lists a checksum for each file, which the future in-app installer can check against.

## 4. Built-in profile updates

What actually happens today:
- **What's sent:** JusPrin asks OrcaSlicer's server for the selected printer's maker (e.g. "Creality"), the OrcaSlicer version (2.4.2), and "JusPrin/2.4.2" as the app name. OrcaSlicer also sees your IP address. No install ID is sent.
- **When:** at start-up, only if the row is on and stealth mode is off. Also every time you switch to a printer from a different maker, and that check ignores both the row and stealth mode. So turning the row off doesn't stop the requests.
- **What comes back:** "not found", for every maker and version I tried (three makers, OrcaSlicer 2.3.0 to 2.5.0). The server currently serves no profile updates, so the row does nothing except send requests.
- JusPrin's built-in profiles are OrcaSlicer 2.4.2's, unchanged apart from one bed-texture image.

Options:
- **A. Keep OrcaSlicer's server and reword the row honestly:** "When you pick a printer, JusPrin asks OrcaSlicer's profile server whether that maker's profiles changed. It sees your IP address, the maker's name and the OrcaSlicer version JusPrin is built on."
- **B. Publish JusPrin's own profile bundles as release files.** The updater asks per maker, which a plain file on GitHub can't answer, so this needs a change to OrcaSlicer's update code, plus a profile release process. Today those bundles would just be copies of OrcaSlicer's files.
- **C. Turn profile updates off for now (recommended).** Profiles arrive with each JusPrin release, which picks up OrcaSlicer's newer profiles at each rebase. No requests go out. The row becomes "Printer and filament profiles update with each JusPrin release."

A and C both need a two-line change in OrcaSlicer's update code so the printer-switch check obeys the row and stealth mode. That's a plain bug fix OrcaSlicer could take too. B is the way to go later if JusPrin starts editing profiles itself.

## What I need from you

1. Approve CI **A**, version **C** and profiles **C**, or pick others.
2. Replace JusPrin 1.x on Windows, or install alongside it?
3. Windows signing: unsigned for 2.0.0, or set up Azure Trusted Signing. And confirm the 1.x Apple secrets still work.
4. Flatpak in 2.0.0 or in 2.0.1?
5. Go-ahead for the dry run: push this branch, add the workflow file to `main`, and run it (several hours of build time). It ends in a draft `v2.0.0` that only collaborators can see, with no tag created. I won't push or publish anything until you say so.

I can turn this into a shareable page if that helps.

<cross-session-message from="local_626ee175-7819-464c-a97e-9269b2eefe7e" name="JusPrin v2 preferences">
Kenneth's answers: (1) yes to all three recommendations: a release workflow started by hand that uploads to a draft release, Version.hpp as the only place the version lives, and profile updates off with profiles shipping in each release; (2) 2.0.0 replaces JusPrin 1.x on Windows; (3) unsigned for the dry run, with signing set up before the public release (Kenneth will check the 1.x Apple secrets himself); (4) Flatpak in 2.0.1, not 2.0.0. (5) The dry run is NOT approved yet: don't push, don't touch main, don't create any release or tag. Go ahead locally on claude/jusprin-release-publishing: fix the packaging so JusPrin no longer installs as OrcaSlicer (keep the OrcaSlicer CMakeLists change to the one additive line), write the workflow, turn profile updates off, and verify everything you can on this machine (including that a local Windows package build has JusPrin's name, IDs and version 2.0.0 and doesn't claim OrcaSlicer's uninstall key). Commit to your branch and report what's ready and exactly what the dry run would do, so Kenneth can approve it in one step.
</cross-session-message>

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard refuses `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` (it reports it as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. Hand build-tree deletion to the user; build trees there contain `resources` symlinks into live worktrees, so unlink those before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.

**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;
a link there holds `.lib` files and breaks their build (LNK1104). Use a separate tree instead: configure
with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`
at a short path such as `C:\b\wsh`, which is a full `libslic3r_gui` build of about 40 minutes. To symbolize a crash
without a debugger, relink with a `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` props file (Link `GenerateDebugInformation`/`GenerateMapFile`),
read the fault offset from the event log (Application, event 1000), and run
`llvm-symbolizer --obj=<exe> --relative-address <offset>` (the symbolizer ships in the MSVC bin dir).

- The in-app browser pane renders a `file://` page as a static snapshot and refuses `screenshot`.
  To look at a rendered page (e.g. a vitest `PREVIEW_OUT` page), serve the directory over a
  throwaway node http server on 127.0.0.1 and navigate to that instead.

**Commits can hang in the `entire` hook (2026-09-25):** `git commit` from an agent session in a worktree
never returned; `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` alone hangs too (60 s, no output,
stdin closed). `--no-verify` does not skip prepare-commit-msg, and hooks must not be bypassed anyway, so
stop after one timed attempt (`timeout 90 git commit ... < /dev/null`), kill the orphaned `entire`
process it leaves behind (`ps -W | grep entire`), and ask Kenneth. Other sessions' commits carry an
`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, so the hook works somewhere; the cause was not found.

**Concurrent harness runs collide on WebView2 (2026-09-25):** every harness exe uses the same WebView2
profile, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JusPrin2\EBWebView`. While another session's harness is running (e.g. a
long `--home-printers-live` fixture run), a second harness fails at once with
`shell_agent_page_handshake_complete FAIL`, and its app log shows `JusPrin agent page failed to load:
The group or resource is not in the correct state`. That is not a page or bundle problem. Check for
`shell_integration_harness.exe` in `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, don't kill another session's
process, and set `$env:WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER='C:\b\<tree>-webview'` for your own runs.

**Scripting on this box (2026-10-06; Python corrected 2026-10-21):** no `python`/`py` on PATH, but Python 3.13 is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\python-3.13.9\python.exe` and runs the prompt suites (`tests/project_prompt`, set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` and `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`). Otherwise use node (`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). Bash heredocs and `node -e "..."` that contain backticks, `${...}` or backslashes get mangled by the shell; write the script to a file with the Write tool and run `node <file>`. The main checkout's build tree `C:\src\JusPrin\build` (VS generator, Release) is fine to build from a session that is working in the main checkout: `cmake --build C:\src\JusPrin\build --config Release --target <targets> -- -m` after `vcvars64.bat`; harness exes there read `resources\` from the source tree, so `npm run build` in `AgentUI` is enough to refresh the Agent page. A touched `Workspace.hpp` rebuild of `libslic3r_gui` + `shell_integration_harness` takes roughly 10 minutes.
