Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-25, Entire CLI 0.11.0): when the committing session has file changes to link,
`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and reads the
answer from `CONIN$`, not stdin. The agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so the open succeeds and the read blocks forever.
`</dev/null` does not help. Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt, which is why it looked intermittent.
The log is buffered, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows nothing until the process exits.
Evidence: handle dump of the hung process showed a `\Device\ConDrv` handle with a blocked synchronous read.
Entire's own Pi integration prefixes agent bash commands with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for this exact reason.
With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` the same hook finished in ~0.3s and added the trailer, 3 of 3 runs; without it, 3 of 3 hung.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.
A separate, real slowdown also exists: an `msbuild -m` build pins all 16 cores (processor queue ~64) and every
`entire` launch then takes 5-20s. That is slow, not hung; don't confuse the two.

**How to apply:** Fixed 2026-09-25: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set as a user env var (HKCU\Environment), so Claude and Codex
shells inherit it after the app restarts (verified in Claude: 3/3 hook runs 0.3s with trailer). If a commit hangs again, first check
`echo $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in the agent shell. Restarting the Claude app: the tray has no Quit, so end all `claude` processes
from a helper launched via WMI (outside Claude's tree) and relaunch with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`.
If one hangs anyway, kill only that commit's `entire` PID; never `--no-verify`. See [[windows-build-machine]].

2026-09-27: with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` already set, a `git merge --no-ff` (merge commit) in a worktree still ran past a
120 s `timeout` -- but the merge commit was already written correctly and nothing was left running. After a timeout, check
`git log -1` and the parents before retrying; a retry would make a second commit. A plain `git commit` minutes earlier took ~seconds.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
APPIMAGETOOLURL="https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/download/continuous/appimagetool-$(uname -m).AppImage"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"


APP_IMAGE="@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@_Linux_V@SoftFever_VERSION@.AppImage"

wget ${APPIMAGETOOLURL} -O ../appimagetool.AppImage
chmod +x ../appimagetool.AppImage

if [ -f /.dockerenv ] ; then # Only run if inside of a Docker Container
sed '0,/AI\x02/{s|AI\x02|\x00\x00\x00|}' -i  ../appimagetool.AppImage
fi

mv @SLIC3R_APP_CMD@ AppRun
chmod +x AppRun

cp resources/images/@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@_192px.png @SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.png
mkdir -p usr/share/icons/hicolor/192x192/apps
cp resources/images/@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@_192px.png usr/share/icons/hicolor/192x192/apps/@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.png
cat <<EOF > com.orcaslicer.@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.desktop
[Desktop Entry]
Name=@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@
Exec=AppRun %F
Icon=@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@
Type=Application
PrefersNonDefaultGPU=true
X-KDE-RunOnDiscreteGpu=true
Categories=Utility;
MimeType=model/stl;application/vnd.ms-3mfdocument;application/prs.wavefront-obj;application/x-amf;
EOF

mkdir -p usr/share/applications
cp com.orcaslicer.@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.desktop usr/share/applications/

mkdir -p usr/share/metainfo
cp "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/flatpak/com.orcaslicer.@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.metainfo.xml" \
  "usr/share/metainfo/com.orcaslicer.@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.metainfo.xml"
cp "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/flatpak/com.orcaslicer.@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.metainfo.xml" \
  "usr/share/metainfo/com.orcaslicer.@SLIC3R_APP_KEY@.appdata.xml"


export ARCH=$(uname -m)

if [ -f /.dockerenv ] ; then # Only run if inside of a Docker Container
  ../appimagetool.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run . $([ -n "${container}" ] && echo '--appimage-extract-and-run')
else
  ../appimagetool.AppImage . $([ -n "${container}" ] && echo '--appimage-extract-and-run')
fi

mv @SLIC3R_APP_KEY@-$(uname -m).AppImage ${APP_IMAGE}
chmod +x ${APP_IMAGE}

# JusPrin's package identity. The top-level CMakeLists.txt includes this file
# just before include(CPack), so each value set here replaces OrcaSlicer's.
#
# Without it the Windows installer calls itself OrcaSlicer by SoftFever,
# version 2.4.2, and uses OrcaSlicer's uninstall key. Because OrcaSlicer turns
# on CPACK_NSIS_ENABLE_UNINSTALL_BEFORE_INSTALL, that installer would first
# uninstall a real OrcaSlicer. With the key "JusPrin", the one JusPrin 1.x
# used, installing 2.x replaces 1.x instead.
#
# The macOS app and the Linux AppImage get the same identity in the release
# workflow (.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml), which renames and edits
# them after the build.

# JusPrin's version lives in one place, Version.hpp; the release workflow
# reads it from there too.
set(_jusprin_version_header "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp")
file(STRINGS "${_jusprin_version_header}" _jusprin_version_line REGEX "kVersion\\[\\] = \"")
if (NOT _jusprin_version_line MATCHES "\"(([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)[^\"]*)\"")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "No kVersion = \"X.Y.Z\" line in ${_jusprin_version_header}")
endif ()
set(JUSPRIN_VERSION "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MAJOR "${CMAKE_MATCH_2}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MINOR "${CMAKE_MATCH_3}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_PATCH "${CMAKE_MATCH_4}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION "${JUSPRIN_VERSION}")

set(CPACK_PACKAGE_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VENDOR "Obico")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_DESCRIPTION_SUMMARY "JusPrin, the AI-piloted 3D printing slicer built on OrcaSlicer")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_HOMEPAGE_URL "https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_INSTALL_DIRECTORY "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_INSTALL_REGISTRY_KEY "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_DISPLAY_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_PACKAGE_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_URL_INFO_ABOUT "${CPACK_PACKAGE_HOMEPAGE_URL}")
# NSIS needs a backslash before the file name, as in OrcaSlicer's value.
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/images\\\\JusPrin.ico")
set(CPACK_NSIS_MUI_ICON "${CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON}")
set(CPACK_NSIS_MUI_UNIICON "${CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON}")
# The executable keeps OrcaSlicer's file name; the shortcuts are called JusPrin.
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_EXECUTABLES "orca-slicer;JusPrin")
# Not used (the generator is NSIS), but never OrcaSlicer's upgrade code.
set(CPACK_WIX_UPGRADE_GUID "4f6d1c0e-6a3b-4b0e-9a57-3d2c8e1f7b42")

string(FIND "${CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME}" "${_jusprin_orca_file_prefix}" _jusprin_prefix_at)

endif ()
string(REPLACE "${_jusprin_orca_file_prefix}" "JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V${JUSPRIN_VERSION}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Turns OrcaSlicer's universal app into JusPrin.app and puts it in a disk image.
#
#   macos_package.sh <OrcaSlicer.app> <version> <output dir>
#
# OrcaSlicer's build names the bundle OrcaSlicer.app with OrcaSlicer's bundle
# identifier, icon and a "JusPrin <build id>" version string. This copies it to
# JusPrin.app and sets JusPrin's identity before anything is signed, because
# editing Info.plist afterwards would break the signature.
#
# Signing: with JUSPRIN_SIGN=1 the app and the disk image are signed with the
# Developer ID certificate in MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID (already in the keychain)
# and notarised with APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID and APP_PWD. Otherwise the app
# gets an ad-hoc signature, which keeps the edited bundle consistent but which
# Gatekeeper rejects for a download: that build is for testing only.
set -euo pipefail

source_app="$1"
version="$2"
out_dir="$3"

script_dir="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd -- "${script_dir}/../../../../.." && pwd)"
entitlements="${repo_root}/scripts/disable_validation.entitlements"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${repo_root}/scripts/retry.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
stage="${work}/dmg"
app="${stage}/JusPrin.app"
dmg="${out_dir}/JusPrin_Mac_universal_V${version}.dmg"
mkdir -p "${stage}" "${out_dir}"
cp -R "${source_app}" "${app}"

plist="${app}/Contents/Info.plist"
buddy=/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy
set_key() {
    "${buddy}" -c "Set :$1 $2" "${plist}" 2>/dev/null || "${buddy}" -c "Add :$1 string $2" "${plist}"
}
set_key CFBundleIdentifier io.obico.jusprin
set_key CFBundleName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleDisplayName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleShortVersionString "${version}"
set_key CFBundleVersion "${version}"
set_key CFBundleGetInfoString "JusPrin ${version}"
cp "${repo_root}/resources/jusprin/images/JusPrin.icns" "${app}/Contents/Resources/images/JusPrin.icns"
set_key CFBundleIconFile images/JusPrin.icns
plutil -lint "${plist}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    codesign --deep --force --verbose --options runtime --timestamp \
        --entitlements "${entitlements}" --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "${app}"
else
    codesign --deep --force --sign - "${app}"
fi
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "${app}"

ln -sfn /Applications "${stage}/Applications"
retry hdiutil create -volname "JusPrin" -srcfolder "${stage}" -ov -format UDZO "${dmg}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    codesign --force --verbose --timestamp --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "${dmg}"
    xcrun notarytool submit "${dmg}" --apple-id "${APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT}" --team-id "${TEAM_ID}" \
        --password "${APP_PWD}" --wait
    xcrun stapler staple "${dmg}"
fi

rm -rf "${work}"
echo "${dmg}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sourceable helper: `retry <cmd...>` runs a command, retrying up to 3 times
# with a 5-minute wait between attempts. Useful for flaky commands such as
# `hdiutil create` intermittently failing with "Resource busy".
retry() {
  local attempt=1 max_attempts=3 delay=300
  until "$@"; do
    if [ "$attempt" -ge "$max_attempts" ]; then
      echo "::error::Command failed after $attempt attempts: $*"
      return 1
    fi
    echo "Attempt $attempt failed: $*. Retrying in $((delay / 60)) minutes..."
    sleep "$delay"
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  done
}

name: JusPrin release build

# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
#
# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      os:
        required: true
        type: string
      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.
      arch:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  cache:
    name: Find the deps cache
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'
      - name: Compute the key
        id: key
        shell: bash
        env:
          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml, so both share one cache.
          cache_os: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && format('macos-{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
          dep_folder: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
        run: |
          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "path=${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Look the cache up
        id: lookup
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

  deps:
    name: Build deps
    needs: cache
    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    with:
      cache-key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
      cache-path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
      valid-cache: false
      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
      # Stops build_deps.yml before it calls OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      build-deps-only: true
    secrets: inherit

  build:
    name: Build JusPrin
    needs: [cache, deps]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.cache.result == 'success' && (needs.deps.result == 'success' || needs.deps.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: Load the deps
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true

      # The same CMake as OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      # The Agent and Home pages are built with npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt).
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # Windows
      - name: Set up MSVC
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: choco install nsis

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: .\build_release_vs.bat slicer

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1 -BuildDir build -Version $env:VERSION `
            -Arch "${{ inputs.arch }}" -OutDir dist

      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them
      # into the universal app and the disk image.
      - name: Prepare the Mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install libtool
          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}"

          sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "Xcode_15.4.app" -exec rm -rf {} +

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -1 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer

      - name: Install the build packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i).

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error

input.content:
name: JusPrin release

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged v<version>. GitHub creates that tag only when the
#   draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update check
#   reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so users see
#   nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released or is not above every
#   released JusPrin version (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
#   1.x used. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so in its
#   title.
#
# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
# jusprin-release/<anything>.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches:
      - 'jusprin-release/**'

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Check the version
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
    steps:
      - name: Only the release publisher
        env:
          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Test the release checks
        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs

      - name: Check the version against the releases
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json"
          node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs check \
            src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Require the release notes
        run: |
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}.md"
          if [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
            echo "::error::Write $notes first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new."
            exit 1
          fi

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.name }}
    needs: prepare
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Windows x64
            os: windows-latest
            arch: x64
          - name: macOS arm64
            os: macos-14
            arch: arm64
          - name: macOS x86_64
            os: macos-14
            arch: x86_64
          - name: Linux x64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            arch: ''
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
    secrets: inherit

  macos:
    name: macOS universal
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: macos-14
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      SIGN: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: Get both architectures
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-macOS-*
          path: mac_bundles
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Join them into the universal app
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/arm64 build/x86_64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_arm64.tar.gz -C build/arm64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_x86_64.tar.gz -C build/x86_64
          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x -1 -a universal -t 10.15

      # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml loads the certificate, with the secret
      # names JusPrin 1.x used.
      - name: Load the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          certificate="$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$certificate"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security default-keychain -s "$keychain"
          security import "$certificate" -P "$P12_PASSWORD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$keychain"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$keychain"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$P12_PASSWORD" "$keychain"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-macOS-universal
          path: dist/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error

  draft:
    name: Upload to the draft release
    needs: [prepare, build, macos]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Optional approval gate: give the "release" environment a required
    # reviewer in the repo settings.
    environment: release
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
      DRAFT_ID: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.draft_id }}
      PRERELEASE: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.prerelease }}
      SIGNED_MACOS: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging

      - name: Collect the files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-*
          path: collected
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Checksums
        run: |
          mkdir dist
          # The per-architecture Mac bundles only feed the universal app.
          find collected -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name 'JusPrin_Mac_bundle_*' -exec cp {} dist/ \;
          (cd dist && sha256sum -- * > SHA256SUMS.txt)
          cat dist/SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Create or update the draft
        run: |
          title="JusPrin $VERSION"
          if [ "$SIGNED_MACOS" != "true" ]; then
            title="$title (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)"
          else
            title="$title (Windows unsigned)"
          fi
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/$VERSION.md"
          prerelease=$([ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ] && echo --prerelease || echo --prerelease=false)
          if [ -z "$DRAFT_ID" ]; then
            gh release create "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft $prerelease \
              --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "$title" --notes-file "$notes"
          else
            # Never touch a published release: release.mjs only reports drafts.
            is_draft=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" --jq .draft)
            if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
              echo "::error::Release $DRAFT_ID is no longer a draft."
              exit 1
            fi
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" \
              -f target_commitish="$GITHUB_SHA" -f name="$title" -F prerelease="$PRERELEASE" \
              -f body="$(cat "$notes")" > /dev/null
            gh release upload "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          fi
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=20" \
            --jq ".[] | select(.tag_name == \"$TAG\") | {name, draft, prerelease, target_commitish, html_url, assets: [.assets[].name]}"

====
Hand OrcaSlicer's update check to JusPrin's, so its request never goes out

The event filter kept OrcaSlicer's update window closed, but OrcaSlicer's
check still asked check-version.orcaslicer.com at every start, sending an
install ID, the version and system details. GUI_App gains a neutral seam:
app_update_check, which runs instead of check_new_version_sf() when set.
JusPrin sets it in attach_shell(), which runs in the MainFrame constructor
before the startup call; the startup call is left to JusPrin's own
schedule, and Help > Check for Updates runs JusPrin's check at once.

With OrcaSlicer's check gone, the filter has nothing to drop; it and its
test are removed.

OrcaSlicer-owned lines: two added to GUI_App.hpp (the member, next to
check_new_version_sf's declaration) and four added at the top of
check_new_version_sf() in GUI_App.cpp. Nothing upstream is deleted or
rewritten. The fork owns a neutral seam; the policy stays in
ShellController.cpp.

version in Version.hpp. It never publishes: GitHub creates the tag when

drafts.

packaging.cmake's CPack identity, JusPrin.app with JusPrin's bundle
identifier, name, version and icon, and an AppImage with JusPrin's
desktop entry. macOS signing and notarisation run only when asked for,
with the secrets JusPrin 1.x used; an unsigned draft says so in its title.

A three-line fix in OrcaSlicer's updater makes the printer-switch check obey that preference and stealth mode too; before, it ignored both. Newer profiles bundled with each JusPrin release still install.
- **e24397f474 — JusPrin installs as JusPrin.** The only change to OrcaSlicer's `CMakeLists.txt` is the one added line, which loads `Packaging/packaging.cmake`. That file sets the name, publisher (Obico) and the uninstall key "JusPrin", so 2.0.0 replaces 1.x. Version 2.0.0 is read from `Version.hpp`. A quick test returned exactly those values, and configuring fails loudly if OrcaSlicer ever renames its installer.
- **ea68ee08d5 — the release workflow.** It builds Windows, macOS and Linux and uploads to a draft release. It never publishes, and an unsigned draft says "UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish" in its title. The version checks pass their 10 tests and pass against JusPrin's real release list. Both workflow files parse and their wiring checks out.

One change from the design: OrcaSlicer's main build job can't be reused unchanged. Its Linux step looks for a file name JusPrin's build never writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer. So the workflow reuses OrcaSlicer's dependency build and build scripts, and only the packaging is JusPrin's. No OrcaSlicer workflow or script is edited.

The rebase simulation against OrcaSlicer's current main shows no conflicts in the files I touched. OrcaSlicer's main has since switched online profile updates off by default; it may conflict with my three-line fix at the next rebase, and dropping the fix then is safe.

Everything Kenneth approved is built and committed on `claude/jusprin-release-publishing` (top commit 85ec57ce9c). Nothing is pushed, `main` is untouched, and no release or tag exists. The dry run is ready for his approval below.

## What's ready
1. **JusPrin no longer installs as OrcaSlicer.** OrcaSlicer's `CMakeLists.txt` got only the one added line, which loads a JusPrin settings file. A local Windows build produced an installer setup that says JusPrin 2.0.0 by Obico and installs to `Program Files\JusPrin`. It uses only the uninstall key "JusPrin", including when it removes the old version first, so 2.0.0 replaces 1.x and never touches OrcaSlicer. "OrcaSlicer", "SoftFever" and "2.4.2" appear nowhere in it except the program's own file name, `orca-slicer.exe`. The portable zip unpacks to a `JusPrin` folder.
2. **Profile updates are off.** JusPrin turns off the setting OrcaSlicer's profile check reads. A three-line fix in OrcaSlicer's code makes the check made on switching printers obey that setting and stealth mode; before, it ignored both. I left OrcaSlicer's master updater switch on, because in this version it also installs the newer profiles that ship with each JusPrin release.
3. **The release workflow.** Kenneth starts it by hand. It builds Windows, macOS and Linux and uploads everything to a draft release named after the version in `Version.hpp`. It refuses a version that is already released or lower than the latest one, and only Kenneth can run it. An unsigned draft is titled "UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish".

One change from the design: OrcaSlicer's main build job can't be reused unchanged. Its Linux step looks for a file name JusPrin's build never writes, and its packaging names everything OrcaSlicer. So the workflow reuses OrcaSlicer's dependency builds and build scripts, and only the packaging is JusPrin's. No OrcaSlicer workflow or script is edited.

## What I verified, and what I couldn't
- **Windows installer:** this machine has no NSIS, the tool that turns the installer script into an .exe. I read the exact script CPack generated, but no real installer was compiled; the dry run will be the first.
- **Profile requests:** the new build saved the setting as off and ran normally; the old build kept it on. I couldn't make either build switch to a maker's printer here, so the printer-switch check wasn't exercised in the app, only read in the code.
- **Release checks:** the version-check tests pass, the check accepts 2.0.0 against the real release list, and the workflow files pass a structural check.
- **Rebase:** a simulation against OrcaSlicer's latest code shows no conflicts in the files I touched.
- **Not testable here:** the macOS packaging, the Linux AppImage step and the workflow itself. They first run in the dry run.

## The dry run, in one approval
1. Push this branch, and push the same commit as a branch named `jusprin-release/dry-run`. That push starts the workflow, so `main` stays untouched. It stops at once unless the pushing GitHub account is `kennethjiang`.
2. GitHub builds Windows x64, macOS (two chips, joined into one app) and Linux x64. The first run also builds the dependencies, so expect several hours of free build time on GitHub; a failure means a fix and a re-run.
3. It creates one draft release, "JusPrin 2.0.0 (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)", for tag `v2.0.0`. It holds the installer, the portable zip, the disk image, the AppImage and a checksum file. Only collaborators can see it, the tag doesn't exist until someone publishes it, and the app's update check never sees drafts.
4. Afterwards I delete the `jusprin-release/dry-run` branch. The draft stays until Kenneth deletes it; a real run reuses it.

## Before the public release
- Replace the placeholder release notes in `Packaging/release-notes/2.0.0.md`; the app shows them under "What's new".
- Run with the macOS signing option ticked once Kenneth has confirmed the Apple secrets.
- Set up Windows signing.

## Found along the way
- **Preferences toggle:** the JusPrin Preferences window is on `claude/prefs-update-check`, not this branch. Its "Update built-in printer and filament profiles" toggle should become a plain line, "Printer and filament profiles update with each JusPrin release", when the two branches meet.
- **Bambu request:** JusPrin still asks Bambu's server for its printer-config bundle at every start unless stealth mode is on. That was out of scope.
- **Windows file properties:** `orca-slicer.exe` shows blank name and version; the old build does too.
- **Mac links:** the Mac app still claims `orcaslicer://` links.

Notes for the other sessions are in [release-publishing-built.md](C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Roaming\Claude\side-session-notes\local_6d12e3c2-d1ec-4939-9214-7be5e8398a61\release-publishing-built.md).

Run it exactly as you described: push claude/jusprin-release-publishing and the same commit as jusprin-release/dry-run, let the workflow build the draft "JusPrin 2.0.0 (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)", don't touch main, don't publish anything, and delete jusprin-release/dry-run afterwards. If a step fails, fix it and re-run without asking, as long as it stays within that scope. Report when the draft exists, with what's in it and anything that failed.

content.text:
The dry run succeeded: every job passed and the workflow created the draft "JusPrin 2.0.0 (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)". But don't publish it. Its tag, `v2.0.0`, already exists as an old OrcaSlicer tag, so publishing would point JusPrin 2.0.0 at OrcaSlicer's 2024 code. Run: [JusPrin release #39895946628](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runs/39895946628), started by `kennethjiang` at commit 85ec57ce9c, about 2.5 hours.

**What the draft should contain:** the Windows x64 installer, the Windows portable zip, the macOS universal disk image (unsigned), the Linux x64 AppImage, and a checksum file. I can't open the draft myself, because drafts need a GitHub login and this machine only has push access. So that list comes from the run's uploaded build files and its passing steps, not from looking at the draft. Kenneth will see it on the Releases page.

**Things that worked for the first time:** the real Windows installer compile, the Linux AppImage step, and the macOS step that turns OrcaSlicer's app into `JusPrin.app` and builds the disk image.

**Nothing went public:**
- The public release list is unchanged; the newest stable release is still `jusprin/v1.4.0`.
- `main` is untouched.
- `jusprin-release/dry-run` is deleted.
- `claude/jusprin-release-publishing` stays pushed.

All four platforms' dependency builds are now cached, so the next run should be much quicker.

**The tag problem.** When JusPrin was forked, the repo kept OrcaSlicer's old version tags, `v2.0.0` through `v2.3.1` and their betas. The draft is for `v2.0.0`. If someone publishes it, GitHub uses the existing tag, which points at an OrcaSlicer commit from March 2024 ("Various profile improvments (#4775)"), not at JusPrin's commit. The download files would be right, but the release's source code would be OrcaSlicer's. JusPrin 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 would hit the same problem.

**Fix, which needs Kenneth's OK because it changes the agreed tag format:**
- Tag new JusPrin releases `jusprin/vX.Y.Z`, as 1.4.0 already was. The app's update check already reads that form.
- Make the version check also refuse any tag that already exists.

That's a small change to `release.mjs` and its tests, then one more dry run. I'd leave the stale `v2.0.0` draft for Kenneth to delete; I can't delete drafts from here.

tell me what the new release process is now.

Here's how a JusPrin release works now. Two caveats first:

- **The release workflow isn't on `jusprin-newui` yet.** It lives on `claude/jusprin-release-publishing` (merged with the latest `jusprin-newui`; the two newest commits aren't pushed yet). Until it's merged in, releases are started from that branch.
- **Only the Run workflow button can sign the Mac app.** Starting a release by pushing a branch always gives an unsigned Mac build. The button only appears once the workflow file is also on the repo's default branch, which is still `main`, the 1.x branch. So before the first signed release, either copy the workflow file to `main` or make the v2 branch the default.

## One-time setup
1. **Apple signing:** confirm the 1.x Apple secrets still work (Kenneth said he'd check). They are `BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64`, `P12_PASSWORD`, `KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD`, `MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID`, `APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT`, `TEAM_ID` and `APP_PWD`.
2. **Windows signing:** not built yet. Until it is, Windows users will see a "Windows protected your PC" warning.
3. **Optional approval gate:** in the repo settings, give the "release" environment a required reviewer (you). The upload then waits for your click.

## Each release
1. **Set the version.** Change the one line in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp` (for example `"2.0.1"`). A label like `"2.1.0-beta1"` makes a test release that only beta users are offered.
2. **Write the notes** in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. They become the release text on GitHub, and the app shows them under "What's new".
3. **Commit and push** to the branch you're releasing from.
4. **Start the build:**
   - Either Actions → "JusPrin release" → Run workflow, ticking "Sign and notarise the macOS app" for a real release.
   - Or push the commit to any branch named `jusprin-release/<name>`, for an unsigned test build.
5. **Wait.** About 1.5 hours with the dependency cache; several hours when the dependencies change.
6. **Review the draft** on the Releases page. Download and try the files, check the notes, and retitle it. An unsigned build is titled "…(UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)".
7. **Click Publish.** That's the only step that makes anything public. GitHub then creates the `jusprin/v<version>` tag, and within a day every running JusPrin offers the update.

## What the workflow does
- **Refuses to start** if:
  - you aren't `kennethjiang`;
  - that version is already released, or lower than the latest release;
  - its `jusprin/v<version>` tag already exists;
  - the notes file is missing.
  
  If the notes are still the placeholder, it only warns.
- **Builds** Windows x64, macOS (both chips joined into one app) and Linux x64. Your files are named and identified as JusPrin, not OrcaSlicer.
- **Uploads to a draft release.** The draft has the Windows installer, the Windows portable zip, the Mac disk image, the Linux AppImage and a checksum file. If you run it again for the same version, the draft's files are replaced.
- **Never publishes or creates a tag.** Users can't see a draft.

## For the first real 2.0.0
1. Push the two unpushed commits.
2. Replace the placeholder notes in `release-notes/2.0.0.md`.
3. Make the Run workflow button available (see the caveat above).
4. Run it with Mac signing ticked. It replaces the files in the existing `jusprin/v2.0.0` draft.
5. Review the draft and publish.

A hand-started workflow builds JusPrin and uploads it to a draft GitHub

  SHA256SUMS.txt to a draft tagged jusprin/v<version>. The version is

  from Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md. Only the release publisher
  may run it; macOS signing runs only when asked for, with JusPrin 1.x's
  Apple secrets; an unsigned draft says so in its title.
- The build reuses OrcaSlicer's build_deps.yml (build-deps-only), its
  cache key and its build scripts. build_orca.yml can't be reused: its
  Linux step expects OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a build
  with JusPrin's app key never writes. No OrcaSlicer workflow is changed.
- Packaging/packaging.cmake gives the Windows installer JusPrin's name,
  publisher (Obico), version, install folder, shortcuts, icon and
  uninstall key "JusPrin" (JusPrin 1.x's, so 2.x replaces 1.x). Before,
  the installer was OrcaSlicer's and, with uninstall-before-install on,
  would have removed a real OrcaSlicer. The macOS app becomes JusPrin.app
  (io.obico.jusprin) and the AppImage gets JusPrin's desktop entry.
- Built-in profiles now change only with a JusPrin release: attach_shell()
